items.name: host/uploadFile · inline
items.summary: Persist a **≤ 8 MiB** payload to host storage in one round-trip by sending it inline as base64. The host decodes, writes to R2 under a per-(user, executa, invoke) key, and returns a short-lived HTTPS GET URL. The plugin holds no R2 credentials and pays no storage of its own. Use this when the payload is already in memory and small; for anything larger use the `negotiate` + `confirm` pair.
items.signature: upload_inline(*, filename: str, mime_type: str, content: bytes, purpose: str | None = None, metadata: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 120.0) -> dict

params.name: filename
params.summary: Logical filename, used for `Content-Disposition` and the storage key suffix.
notes: Empty → `UPLOAD_INVALID_REQUEST` (`-32203` on the wire, `-32204` in Nexus gate — see Errors).

The host runs `_safe_filename(filename)` before setting `Content-Disposition`; unsafe characters are stripped. The original name is **not** preserved in the storage key — keys are opaque (`exec-uploads/{env}/{user_uuid}/{tool_id}/{invoke_id}/{purpose}/{sha-suffix}`).

params.name: mime_type
notes: Validated against the host's hard-coded denylist only (executables, `image/svg+xml`) — the per-token MIME allowlist was removed (forum #218): any non-blocked type is accepted, Office formats included. Reject → `UPLOAD_MIME_REJECTED` (`-32205` wire / `-32210` gate).

Drives `Content-Disposition`, which is **signed into every download URL** (client cannot strip it): `image/*` / `audio/*` / `video/*` (except SVG) and `application/pdf` → `inline`; everything else → `attachment`. Pick `text/plain` over `application/octet-stream` when the real type is known — readers like `sheet_read` / `doc_read` select parsers by MIME.

params.name: content
params.summary: Raw bytes; the SDK base64-encodes before sending (you do NOT pre-encode).
notes: **Hard cap 8 MiB** raw (`INLINE_MAX_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024`); larger → `UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (`-32204` wire / `-32211` gate). The SDK pre-checks (`MAX_INLINE_BYTES`) and raises `UploadError` locally to avoid wasting a round-trip.
Empty bytes → `UPLOAD_INVALID_REQUEST`.
The wire payload is ~4/3× larger than `content` due to base64; budget your `_clientTimeoutS` for the upstream transfer.

params.name: purpose
notes: Defaults to `"user_artifact"` server-side when omitted (see `executa_upload_gate.handle_upload_inline_request`).

Validated against `ALLOWED_PURPOSES = {"image_input", "image_reference", "user_artifact"}` AND against `upload_token.allowed_purposes` when set. Reject → `UPLOAD_PURPOSE_REJECTED` (`-32206` wire / `-32212` gate).
Used for billing categorisation and TTL policy (image purposes may have shorter retention).

params.name: metadata
params.summary: Opaque metadata echoed into the storage row.
notes: Do not store secrets — visible to user in account audit log.

params.name: timeout
params.summary: SDK-side per-call deadline; injected as `_clientTimeoutS`. Channel cap is `UPLOAD_MAX_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S = 300s`.

returns.desc:
Built by `executa_upload_gate` from `UploadResult`:
• `r2_key: str` — opaque storage key; pass back to `confirm` (or `files/download_url` if you've previously created one) to re-presign later.
• `mime_type: str` — echoed from input.
• `bytes_size: int` — decoded byte count (post-base64-decode).
• `download_url: str` — transient HTTPS GET URL, **~30 min TTL** (`R2_TRANSIENT_PRESIGN_EXPIRY = 1800s`).
• `expires_in: int` — seconds until `download_url` 403s.

The SDK wraps the call result with `{"mode": "inline", ...}` for client-side mode discrimination.

errors.name: UPLOAD_NOT_GRANTED
errors.desc: User has not enabled `upload_grant` for this Executa, or the executa is disabled, or manifest is missing `host_capabilities: ["host.upload"]`.

errors.name: QUOTA_EXCEEDED
errors.desc: User plan storage quota exhausted.

errors.name: INVALID_REQUEST
errors.desc: Missing `filename` / `mime_type` / `content_b64`, malformed base64, or `executa_tool_id` / `tool_invoke_id` mismatch with the token. Note: Nexus gate uses `-32204` for this; matrix-side SDK uses `-32203`. Catch by `error_name`, not numeric code.

errors.name: TOO_LARGE
errors.desc: Decoded payload exceeds 8 MiB (SDK pre-check) or token's `max_file_bytes` (server-side). Gate code: `-32211`.

errors.name: MIME_REJECTED
errors.desc: MIME malformed or on the host's hard denylist (executables, `image/svg+xml`). The per-token allowlist was removed (forum #218) — any other type is accepted. Gate code: `-32210`.

errors.name: PURPOSE_REJECTED
errors.desc: `purpose` not in `upload_token.allowed_purposes` or not in the global allowlist. Gate code: `-32212`.

errors.name: STORAGE_ERROR
errors.desc: R2 `put_object` failed; the upload was not persisted. Safe to retry. Gate code: `-32203`.

errors.name: TIMEOUT
errors.desc: SDK-local timeout. Gate code for upstream timeout: `-32205` (different number — match `error_name`).

errors.name: USER_DENIED
errors.desc: User explicitly declined an in-the-moment confirm prompt.

errors.name: MAX_FILES_EXCEEDED
errors.desc: Per-invoke rolling counter `upl:invoke:{tool_invoke_id}` exhausted `upload_token.max_files` (default 16). Gate code: `-32206`.

items.example:
from executa_sdk import HostUploadClient, UploadError, UPLOAD_ERR_TOO_LARGE

upload = HostUploadClient()

async def persist_screenshot(invoke_id: str, png: bytes) -> str:
    try:
        res = await upload.upload_inline(
            filename="screenshot.png",
            mime_type="image/png",
            content=png,                       # raw bytes; SDK base64s for you
            purpose="user_artifact",
            timeout=60.0,
        )
    except UploadError as e:
        if e.code == UPLOAD_ERR_TOO_LARGE:
            # SDK pre-checked 8 MiB cap. Switch to negotiate + confirm.
            return await persist_via_presigned(invoke_id, png)
        raise
    return res["download_url"]                  # ~30 min TTL; persist r2_key for repeat presigns
limitations: **8 MiB hard cap** on raw bytes (`INLINE_MAX_BYTES`). For larger payloads use `host/uploadFile · negotiate` + `· confirm`. The SDK pre-checks (`MAX_INLINE_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024`) so you don't burn a round-trip.
**Returned `download_url` expires in ~30 min** (`R2_TRANSIENT_PRESIGN_EXPIRY = 1800s`). Persist the `r2_key` if you'll need to re-mint the URL later; do not store the URL itself in long-lived state.
**No de-duplication** — uploading the same bytes twice creates two R2 objects and counts twice against the user's quota. Memoise client-side.

**Per-invoke quotas are enforced** — `upload_token.max_files` (default 16) and `max_total_bytes` (default 80 MiB) are shared across `inline` + `confirm` within one `invoke_id`. Plan accordingly for batch operations.
**Error code numbering diverges between the Agent SDK and the Nexus gate** (see the Errors table). Always switch on `error_name` strings, not raw codes.

items.name: host/uploadFile · negotiate
items.direction: Plugin → Agent → Nexus REST (presign) → returns PUT URL
items.summary: Step 1 of the two-phase upload for payloads larger than `inline`'s 8 MiB cap (or whenever you want to stream from a file without buffering it all in memory): the host signs an R2 PUT URL bound to a specific key + content-type, the plugin uploads bytes directly to R2, then calls `confirm` to register the object. The PUT URL never expires until the TTL, but the plugin still holds no long-term R2 credentials.
items.signature: negotiate(*, filename: str, mime_type: str, size_bytes: int, purpose: str | None = None, metadata: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 120.0) -> dict

params.name: filename
notes: Empty → `UPLOAD_INVALID_REQUEST`. Not stored in the key path; opaque key only.

params.name: mime_type
params.summary: MIME type; **must match exactly** what the plugin will send as `Content-Type` on the PUT (R2 enforces this).
notes: Validated against the host hard denylist only (MIME allowlist removed); reject → `MIME_REJECTED`.
Returned in `headers["Content-Type"]` so the plugin can copy it verbatim into the PUT request.

params.name: size_bytes
params.summary: Expected byte count of the upload; used for quota pre-check only.
notes: Wire field name on the REST body is `expected_bytes`; the SDK accepts the friendlier `size_bytes`.
Must be `> 0` → otherwise `UPLOAD_INVALID_REQUEST`.
If `size_bytes > upload_token.max_file_bytes` (default 20 MiB) → `UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (`-32204` wire) immediately, before any R2 round-trip — saves bandwidth.
R2 does **not** enforce the value on PUT; over-shipping bytes succeeds at the object store but the `confirm` step will rejet if `head_object.ContentLength > max_file_bytes`.

params.name: purpose
params.summary: Same purpose tag and validation as `inline.purpose`. Defaults to `user_artifact`.

params.name: metadata
params.summary: Opaque metadata; echoed into storage row.

params.name: timeout
params.summary: SDK timeout for the *negotiate* round-trip only (typically <1s). The subsequent R2 PUT is plugin-managed and not bounded by this.

returns.desc:
Built from `NegotiateResult`:
• `r2_key: str` — opaque object key, must be passed back to `confirm`.
• `put_url: str` — presigned R2 PUT URL, valid for `expires_in` seconds (default **300s / 5 min**, `DEFAULT_PRESIGN_PUT_EXPIRY`).
• `expires_in: int` — TTL in seconds. The PUT must complete (i.e. R2 returns 200) before this elapses.
• `headers: dict` — exact request headers the plugin must include on the PUT; today this is `{"Content-Type": mime_type}`. Omitting them causes R2 to 403.

The SDK wraps with `{"mode": "negotiate", ...}`.

errors.name: UPLOAD_NOT_GRANTED
errors.desc: Same as inline.

errors.name: QUOTA_EXCEEDED
errors.desc: User plan quota exhausted (pre-check before signing).

errors.name: INVALID_REQUEST
errors.desc: Missing `filename` / `mime_type` / `size_bytes`, non-positive `size_bytes`, or token mismatch.

errors.name: TOO_LARGE
errors.desc: `size_bytes > max_file_bytes`.

errors.name: MIME_REJECTED
errors.desc: MIME outside allowlist.

errors.name: PURPOSE_REJECTED
errors.desc: Purpose outside allowlist.

errors.name: STORAGE_ERROR
errors.desc: R2 `generate_presigned_url` failed (rare; mostly creds/clock skew).

errors.name: MAX_FILES_EXCEEDED
errors.desc: Per-invoke files counter exhausted (note: negotiate alone does NOT increment the counter; confirm does).

items.example:
import httpx
from executa_sdk import HostUploadClient

upload = HostUploadClient()

async def upload_large_video(invoke_id: str, video_bytes: bytes) -> dict:
    # 1. Negotiate — get a presigned PUT URL.
    neg = await upload.negotiate(
        filename="capture.mp4",
        mime_type="video/mp4",
        size_bytes=len(video_bytes),
        purpose="user_artifact",
    )
    # 2. PUT direct to R2. Must use exact headers + within `expires_in` seconds.
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as http:
        r = await http.put(neg["put_url"], content=video_bytes, headers=neg["headers"], timeout=300.0)
        r.raise_for_status()
    # 3. Confirm — get a transient download URL.
    return await upload.confirm(r2_key=neg["r2_key"])
limitations: **PUT URL TTL is 5 min** (`DEFAULT_PRESIGN_PUT_EXPIRY = 300`). For very large uploads on slow links, the plugin must complete within this window; otherwise re-negotiate (and abandon the stale URL — R2 won't 'time out' the URL, the signature just becomes invalid).

**`size_bytes` is advisory at sign time, enforced at confirm time.** Over-shipping bytes succeeds at R2 but `confirm` rejects with `UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (`head_object.ContentLength > max_file_bytes`). Under-shipping is allowed but wastes the quota you reserved.
**Headers must match exactly** — copy `headers` verbatim into the PUT. Adding or omitting any of them invalidates the signature.

**Negotiate does not count against `max_files`** — only `confirm` does, since negotiate may be cancelled. This means a misbehaving plugin can spam negotiate; the host throttles via the `upload_token` TTL (10 min) and Nexus's per-user rate-limit middleware.

**No partial / resumable uploads** — R2 multipart is not exposed to plugins. If your payload is larger than `max_file_bytes` (default 20 MiB, max 100 MiB by user grant), split it into multiple files application-side.

items.name: host/uploadFile · confirm
items.direction: Plugin → Agent → Nexus REST → R2 HEAD
items.summary: Step 2 of the two-phase upload: after a successful R2 PUT, register the object with the host. The host HEADs R2 to verify the bytes landed, increments the per-invoke files+bytes counters, and returns a short-lived download URL — symmetric to the `inline` result. Must be called within the same `tool_invoke_id` that minted the upload_token.
items.signature: confirm(*, r2_key: str, timeout: float = 120.0) -> dict

params.name: r2_key
params.summary: The exact `r2_key` returned by the preceding `negotiate` call.
notes: Validated server-side: must start with `exec-uploads/{env}/{user_uuid}/` AND contain `/{executa_tool_id}/` AND `/{tool_invoke_id}/`. Cross-invoke or cross-tool reuse → `UPLOAD_INVALID_REQUEST` (`-32203`).
If R2 has no object at the key (PUT failed, never happened, or expired) → `UPLOAD_NOT_FOUND` (`-32212` wire / `-32213` gate). Treat as 'retry the negotiate+PUT pair'.

params.name: timeout
params.summary: SDK-side per-call deadline; this round-trip is just one R2 HEAD plus a presign — typically completes in <1s.

returns.desc:
Same shape as `inline` (also `UploadResult`):
• `r2_key: str` — echoed.
• `mime_type: str` — read from R2 `head_object.ContentType` (so this is the value that was on the PUT, not what was originally negotiated; usually identical).
• `bytes_size: int` — `head_object.ContentLength`; the authoritative byte count.
• `download_url: str` — transient HTTPS GET URL, **~30 min TTL** (`R2_TRANSIENT_PRESIGN_EXPIRY`).
• `expires_in: int` — seconds until `download_url` 403s.

The SDK wraps with `{"mode": "confirm", ...}`. This call **increments** the per-invoke files (+1) and bytes (+`bytes_size`) counters — if it pushes either past the token cap, the call rolls back the increment and raises `UPLOAD_MAX_FILES_EXCEEDED` / `UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES_EXCEEDED`.

errors.name: UPLOAD_NOT_GRANTED
errors.desc: Same as inline.

errors.name: INVALID_REQUEST
errors.desc: `r2_key` prefix doesn't match the calling invoke, or doesn't contain the executa tool id.

errors.name: TOO_LARGE
errors.desc: `head_object.ContentLength > max_file_bytes` — plugin shipped more bytes than negotiated.

errors.name: STORAGE_ERROR
errors.desc: R2 HEAD or presign failed (transient).

errors.name: MAX_FILES_EXCEEDED
errors.desc: Confirming would push per-invoke files counter past `max_files`. Confirm is what charges the counter, not negotiate.

errors.name: NOT_FOUND
errors.desc: R2 has no object at `r2_key` — PUT failed silently or was never attempted. Wire code may also appear as `-32213` from the gate.

items.example:
# Continued from `negotiate` example.
result = await upload.confirm(r2_key=neg["r2_key"])
#  →  {"mode": "confirm", "r2_key": "...", "mime_type": "video/mp4",
#       "bytes_size": 7340032, "download_url": "https://...", "expires_in": 1800}
limitations: **Confirm is what charges quota** — failed PUTs without confirm leave orphan R2 objects that the host janitors-up via a separate sweep job, but they don't count against the user's per-invoke caps. Conversely, never call confirm without a successful PUT — you'll get `UPLOAD_NOT_FOUND` and waste a request.
**`r2_key` is per-invoke** — you cannot 'borrow' an r2_key obtained in a previous `invoke` call; the prefix check rejects it. Re-uploading the same payload across invokes is the correct pattern.
**Result `mime_type` may differ from negotiate input** if the plugin shipped a different `Content-Type` header on the PUT (R2 records whatever was sent). Don't rely on these being identical.
